scope: Full Power Stack daily research refresh across US, Hong Kong/China and Malaysia. All tracked categories and current holdings rescanned; creator/social material remains hypothesis-only until independently verified.
whatIsNewNow: Middle East energy risk escalated again: Iran targeted 10 ships near Hormuz after the US sank five Iranian oil tankers; Brent settled above $100 at $101.21. The energy theme remains dominant, but EIA's Sep 9 STEO explicitly expects alternative routes and gradually improving Hormuz flows to restore Middle East production toward pre-conflict averages by 2Q27, so the thesis remains two-sided rather than a permanent $100+ crude call.

EIA materially raised the importance of refined products: US distillate inventories are forecast below 100m barrels and below the five-year low through much of 2027, with 2026 retail diesel now forecast at $5.07/gal. This strengthens refiners, logistics and integrated energy relative to simple crude beta.

US power demand received fresh official confirmation: EIA forecasts record 2026 electricity sales of 4,135 BkWh and 4,211 BkWh in 2027, driven by data centres and manufacturing. This supports grid/generation/cooling names while EIA also explicitly acknowledges Texas data-centre connection screening.

Qualcomm enters NEW PRIORITY RESEARCH as a differentiated AI-infrastructure/physical-AI candidate after a multi-generation Amazon collaboration covering custom AI inference silicon and up-to-1.6T optical connectivity. Reuters reports potential Amazon purchases up to $60bn plus warrants; Qualcomm targets >$15bn data-centre revenue by FY2029. It is research-only / do-not-chase pending valuation and execution work.

Agriculture/weather moves higher: Argentina is filling Black Sea/European grain gaps with record Aug-Sep corn exports, while super-El Nino conditions are driving exceptional Indonesian wildfire/heat stress. This is early evidence of weather + trade-route food inflation, not yet proof of broad crop losses.
Gold/silver strengthened despite high long yields, but PPI/CPI remain the next test. Strategic precious-metal demand is improving while tactical entries remain rate-sensitive.
